title: Machine-Learning Adaptivity, DFT-Level Accuracy, and Semi-Empirical Quantum-Chemistry Speed with Neural-Network Extended Tight-Binding
authors: Yufan Xia; Albert Thie; Joshua Soon; Giuseppe Maria Junior Barca
one_liner_zh: 该文提出神经网络扩展紧束缚方法（NN-xTB），通过神经网络修正半经验量子化学哈密顿量以提升精度，虽涉及分子模拟和AI方法，但未聚焦蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，仅方法上对分子力场/量子化学模拟有潜在迁移价值。
abstract: Fast, general, and interpretable quantum accuracy remains a challenge. To address it, we introduce Neural Network Extended Tight-Binding (NN-xTB), a Hamiltonian-preserving scheme that augments the GFN2-xTB operator with small, bounded, environment-dependent shifts to a compact set of physically interpretable parameters predicted by neural network. NN-xTB confines learning to atom/shell local parameters and to a few global scalings, enhancing local chemical adaptivity while preserving analytic long-range limits, native charge and spin treatment, and self-consistency, and ensuring that all observables are derived from a single adapted electronic state. Across complementary benchmarks, NN-xTB attains DFT-like accuracy at near-xTB cost. On GMTKN55 it achieves a WTMAD-2 of 4 kcal/mol (versus 25 kcal/mol for GFN2-xTB and 9.3 kcal/mol for g-xTB). Relative to strong equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), NN-xTB yields the lowest force MAE on eight out of ten rMD17 molecules and delivers 10-40% RMSE reductions on large subsets of MACEOFF23 and SPICE. Under temperature shift on the 3BPA dataset, errors remain substantially below competing MLIPs up to 1200 K, indicating stronger out-of-distribution generalization. On VQM24, the vibrational-frequency MAE drops from 200.6 cm^{-1} (GFN2-xTB) to 12.7 cm^{-1} (more than 90% reduction). The neural component adds less than 20% wall-time overhead, preserving the throughput that motivates semi-empirical quantum methods. By adapting the Hamiltonian rather than directly regressing energies or forces, NN-xTB bridges much of the accuracy gap to DFT while retaining interpretability, correct asymptotics, and robustness, offering a practical route to quantum-accurate molecular simulation and modeling at scale.
abstract_zh: 快速、通用且可解释的量子精度仍是一项挑战。为解决此问题，我们引入了神经网络扩展紧束缚（Neural Network Extended Tight-Binding, NN-xTB），这是一种哈密顿量保持方案，通过神经网络预测的少量有界、环境依赖的偏移，增强GFN2-xTB算符中一组紧凑的物理可解释参数。NN-xTB将学习限制在原子/壳层局部参数及少数全局缩放上，增强局部化学适应性，同时保留解析长程极限、原生电荷与自旋处理及自洽性，确保所有可观测量均源自单一适配的电子态。在互补基准测试中，NN-xTB以接近xTB的计算成本达到DFT级精度。在GMTKN55上，其WTMAD-2为4 kcal/mol（相比之下，GFN2-xTB为25 kcal/mol，g-xTB为9.3 kcal/mol）。相对于强等变机器学习原子间势（MLIPs），NN-xTB在rMD17的十个分子中八个上取得最低力MAE，并在MACEOFF23和SPICE的大子集上实现10-40%的RMSE降低。在3BPA数据集上的温度偏移测试中，误差在高达1200 K时仍显著低于竞争性MLIPs，表明其具有更强的分布外泛化能力。在VQM24上，振动频率MAE从200.6 cm^{-1}（GFN2-xTB）降至12.7 cm^{-1}（减少超过90%）。神经组件增加不到20%的墙钟时间开销，保持了半经验量子方法所追求的吞吐量。通过调整哈密顿量而非直接回归能量或力，NN-xTB弥合了与DFT之间的大部分精度差距，同时保留可解释性、正确渐近性和鲁棒性，为大规模量子精确分子模拟与建模提供了实用途径。
